claims.reason: It is an argument. It is instance-implicit, and 𝕜 is an argument because it appears in `fderiv 𝕜` and `DifferentiableAt 𝕜`. Nothing in the statement needs it to elaborate: `DifferentiableAt 𝕜`, `fderiv 𝕜` and the operator norm on `E →L[𝕜] G` only need `NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜` and the normed-space instances. The current proof uses it only to build `RCLike 𝕜` and a real structure on G inside `norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le` (line 426). The reviewer's direct argument works over any nontrivially normed field. Let g(t) = f(x + t•(y−x)). By `hs.mapsTo_lineMap`, g maps [0,1] into s. f is continuous at each point of s (`DifferentiableAt.continuousAt`), so g is continuous on [0,1]. Fix t ∈ [0,1) and let L = fderiv 𝕜 f (g t). As z → t⁺, w = (z−t)•v → 0 in E. `HasFDerivAt` gives ‖f(g t + w) − f(g t) − L w‖ = o(‖w‖), and `le_opNorm` gives ‖L w‖ ≤ C(z−t)‖v‖. So for any r > C‖v‖, eventually (hence frequently, since 𝓝[>] t is NeBot) slope(‖g · − g 0‖) t z ≤ ‖g z − g t‖/(z−t) < r. `image_norm_le_of_liminf_right_slope_norm_lt_deriv_boundary` (line 224) exists and only needs `[NormedAddCommGroup E]`. Apply it with f' = C‖v‖ and B(t) = (C‖v‖+ε)t, which is continuous and has derivative C‖v‖+ε > f'. This gives ‖f y − f x‖ ≤ C‖v‖ + ε for every ε > 0, which proves the claim. No RCLike structure is used. A sanity check agrees: a real normed space E that is also a compatible 𝕜-normed space forces 𝕜 to be archimedean, or E to be trivial. Even in exotic cases such as 𝕜 = ℚ with G a ℚ-normed space without a real structure, the direct argument above still applies.
